diagnosis: Deadlock due to lock inversion between queue_lock and stats_lock, exacerbated by threads waiting on a shared barrier while holding one of these locks, creating a circular dependency where neither can proceed because each holds a lock the other needs before reaching the barrier.
root_cause: The worker thread acquires queue_lock then waits on the barrier while still holding queue_lock, needing stats_lock which the monitor holds; simultaneously, the monitor thread acquires stats_lock then waits on the same barrier while holding stats_lock, needing queue_lock which the worker holds. This creates a classic hold-and-wait deadlock scenario involving both mutex inversion and barrier synchronization.
reasoning_summary: Both threads were observed holding one lock while waiting on the barrier and trying to acquire the other lock held by the opposing thread. Moving the barrier wait outside the critical sections eliminates the hold-and-wait condition while preserving the original intent of the overlap test via post-lock acquisition of the secondary mutex.
expected_effect: Eliminates the circular wait condition by ensuring no thread holds any mutex while blocking on the barrier, allowing both threads to reach the barrier and proceed without deadlock.
risk_notes: The reordering changes the timing of stats_lock and queue_lock acquisition relative to the barrier, but since the barrier is only used for test overlap and the secondary mutex is immediately acquired and released afterward, functional behavior for job processing and inspection remains preserved.
Potential minor performance impact due to extra lock/unlock pairs in the overlap case, but this is acceptable for a test hook and does not affect correctness.
